macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street futures fall as AI concerns and Fed signals weigh
items.summary: U.S. stock futures declined, with Dow futures down 0.2%, S&P 500 futures down 0.76%, and Nasdaq 100 futures down 1.63%. Investor sentiment weakened after Anthropic shares retreated following a strong debut and Federal Reserve officials signaled support for further rate increases.[1]

items.title: U.S. stocks extend six-session sell-off
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 2%, the Dow dropped 2.2%, and the Nasdaq 100 declined 2.2% as concerns over AI valuations, tighter monetary policy, and market liquidity intensified. AMD fell 7.7% after a short-seller report, while Nvidia lost 3.3%.[2]

items.title: Fed tightening expectations increase
items.summary: Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson said another interest-rate increase may be needed because inflation remains too high. Markets were pricing a 98.4% probability of a December rate hike, while higher Treasury yields and a stronger dollar pressured risk assets.[1]

items.title: U.S. manufacturing weakens as price pressures rise
items.summary: The Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index fell to 6.3 in November from 20.9, with new orders entering contraction, while prices paid rose sharply. Initial jobless claims increased to 203,000 and continuing claims rose to 1.763 million.[2]

items.title: Anthropic IPO fails to stabilize AI trade
items.summary: Anthropic shares initially surged after pricing its IPO at $83 per share, but the stock later retreated, renewing investor concerns about AI-sector valuations and the sustainability of elevated technology spending.[1][2]

items.title: Oil prices decline on supply-surplus expectations
items.summary: Brent crude fell 1.6% and was headed for a third consecutive weekly decline as shipments through the Strait of Hormuz returned toward prewar levels and markets anticipated excess supply.[1]

items.title: Asian equities fall after Wall Street losses
items.summary: Asian stocks weakened as global risk aversion spread from the U.S., driven by AI-sector volatility, concerns about tighter Federal Reserve policy, and liquidity pressures. Japan’s Nikkei 225 was an exception, closing 0.71% higher.[2][3]

items.title: Insmed raises outlook on strong Brinsupri prospects
items.summary: Insmed shares rose 20.58% after the company raised its 2026 guidance and projected peak sales of more than $7 billion for Brinsupri.[3]

items.title: PDD Holdings beats earnings expectations
items.summary: PDD Holdings gained 11.04% after reporting better-than-expected third-quarter earnings, alongside easing concerns about European regulatory pressure on its Temu platform.[3]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $62,000 as crypto sell-off deepens
items.summary: Bitcoin traded below $62,000, down about 2.6% over 24 hours, while ether fell 3.7% to roughly $1,734. Solana, BNB and XRP also declined, and crypto liquidations across major exchanges reached about $402 million.

items.title: CFTC outlines pathway for blockchain-based retail derivatives venues
items.summary: CFTC Chair Michael Selig said blockchain-based platforms could enter the U.S. retail derivatives market by obtaining exchange registration or partnering with an existing registered venue, while meeting the same regulatory requirements as traditional exchanges.

items.title: Singapore issues $77.5 million of tokenized central-bank bills
items.summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore issued S$100 million of four-week tokenized central-bank bills on a distributed ledger and settled them using wholesale central bank digital currency. Five banks participated, with demand exceeding twice the amount offered.

items.title: Hong Kong regulator flags Hyperliquid licensing concerns
items.summary: Hong Kong’s securities regulator said Hyperliquid lacked a local license and may have promoted its trading services to investors in the city.

items.title: Loopring shuts down decentralized exchange and AMM
items.summary: Loopring announced the closure of its decentralized exchange and automated market maker, citing weak adoption and technological obsolescence in the evolving zk-rollup sector.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon frontier model
items.summary: Google reportedly released Gemini 4 Neon for complex software development, knowledge work, and scientific reasoning. The model is offered through an API with a one-million-token context window and configurable reasoning levels.[2][5]

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-6.2 Astra for demanding professional and reasoning workloads and GPT-6.2 Sol as a lower-cost option for everyday tasks. Reports also describe lower pricing for the new models.[1][4]

items.title: Microsoft expands its in-house AI model lineup
items.summary: Microsoft announced new first-party models spanning coding, cybersecurity, and real-time speech. MAI-Code-2 is generally available in GitHub Copilot, while other models have more limited or preview availability.[3][5]

items.title: Microsoft puts Maia200 AI accelerator into scaled production
items.summary: Microsoft reportedly moved its second-generation Maia200 accelerator into scaled production for data-center deployment. The company says it delivers a 1.7-times improvement in tokens per watt.[3]

items.title: US export restrictions threaten delays to Tencent’s next LLM
items.summary: Tencent said tightened US restrictions on overseas access to advanced Nvidia hardware will make development of its next large language model more difficult. The company expects China to rely increasingly on domestically produced semiconductors.[2]

items.title: Anthropic reportedly targets major IPO valuation
items.summary: Anthropic was reportedly positioned for an initial public offering valued at approximately $1.4 trillion, although the available report provides limited additional detail.[2]

items.title: Anthropic claims Claude solved two black-hole physics problems
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly said its Claude Fable 5.2 model solved two open problems in black-hole physics. The available report does not provide technical details or independent validation.[2]

items.title: OpenAI reports accelerating internal AI use
items.summary: OpenAI published findings indicating that AI use within its research organization is rising rapidly and that agents are completing longer tasks, while human researchers remain involved. The company also urged AI labs to disclose recursive self-improvement efforts.[3]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches worldwide
items.summary: Rockstar’s Grand Theft Auto VI reportedly launched on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, returning the series to Vice City. Early coverage highlights exceptionally strong reviews and substantial player interest.[5]

items.title: GTA VI drives major streaming surge
items.summary: Early reports say Grand Theft Auto VI generated unusually high livestream viewership after launch, with estimates claiming millions of concurrent viewers across major platforms. Those figures and sales estimates remain preliminary.[4]

items.title: Ubisoft creates generative-AI studio Motherbrain
items.summary: Ubisoft announced Motherbrain, a subsidiary focused on generative AI for gameplay, including smart NPCs, AI game masters and other creator tools. The move comes alongside further reported job cuts at Ubisoft studios.[7]

items.title: League of Legends overhaul announced for 2027
items.summary: Riot Games reportedly unveiled League of Legends: New Dawn and announced a major overhaul planned for 2027, accompanied by a debut trailer.[2]

items.title: Paradox Interactive CEO Fredrik Wester steps down
items.summary: Fredrik Wester reportedly left his position as chief executive of Paradox Interactive, marking a leadership change at the publisher known for strategy franchises.[2]

items.title: Counter-Strike 2 restores Cobblestone to matchmaking
items.summary: Valve reportedly returned Cobblestone to Counter-Strike 2 matchmaking while removing Boulder, Fachwerk and Shelter. The update also opened the PGL Singapore 2026 Major hub and related Pick’Em features.[5]

items.title: VALORANT patch 13.10 adds replay bookmarks
items.summary: Riot’s VALORANT 13.10 update reportedly adds replay match bookmarks, changes Sentinel utility cooldowns and revises aspects of the Gauntlet: Glitched mode.[5]

items.title: New Switch games announced and release delayed
items.summary: Recent announcements include Dual Orb Collection and Saihate Station: Twilight Edition for Nintendo Switch, while Caladrius 2/Dark Element was reportedly delayed to January 27, 2027.[1]
